patch.summary:
Choose Getscreen.me only if your buying job matches “Remote desktop / screen-share adjacent tool — Free (1 user, ≤2 devices); Standard from $5/” rather than Office Timeline's shape. Choose Office Timeline only if your buying job matches “PowerPoint-native timeline / Gantt specialist (now Lucen Timeline) — Free add-in; Lite fro” rather than Getscreen.me's shape. Workflow advantage: Getscreen.me leans remote-support-access; Office Timeline leans timeline-reporting, project-tracking. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Getscreen.me is Remote desktop / screen-share adjacent tool — Free (1 user, ≤2 devices); Standard from $5/user + device fees.; Office Timeline is PowerPoint-native timeline / Gantt specialist (now Lucen Timeline) — Free add-in; Lite from $9/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Getscreen.me (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Office Timeline (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Getscreen.me-leaning remote-support-access vs Office Timeline-leaning timeline-reporting, project-tracking.
- Researched limits: Getscreen.me — Adjacent remote-access tool — not a project management platform; Office Timeline — Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management.

Limitations — Getscreen.me: Adjacent remote-access tool — not a project management platform; Hybrid user + device pricing means TCO rises with device count; Office Timeline: Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management; Centre of gravity is PowerPoint presentation timelines, not live team task execution.
